screens.prompt: In B7, read the units for the region in B5 and the quarter in B6 from the grid B2:D4.

hints.syntax: =INDEX(B2:D4,MATCH(B5,A2:A4,0),MATCH(B6,B1:D1,0)): the grid, then a row, then a column.
hints.func-index: INDEX needs both numbers. With only the row it reads along the first column of B2:D4 and ignores the quarter.
hints.func-match: One MATCH looks down the region column, the other looks across the quarter header row. INDEX waits for both.
hints.match-exact: Both lists are in the order they were typed, so both MATCH calls need 0.
hints.require-ref: Read the region from B5 and the quarter from B6 so the sheet drives the answer.
hints.value: South is the second region down and Q3 is the third column across, so INDEX reads 130.
hints.error: A quarter missing from B1:D1, or a region missing from A2:A4, gives #N/A.

reject.why: one bracket is still open, so nothing computes
the right cell, but both positions are hardcoded instead of looked up
answers 2, the row South sits on, not the units in it
approximate match on an unsorted region column
the quarter headers are in row 1, so searching row 2 finds no Q3
the region and quarter typed into the formula, so a change in B6 or B7 never reaches the answer
steps one column before the month that was matched, so the total is one month early

docs.explain:
Two MATCH calls answer two separate questions. South is second in A2:A4, so the first returns 2. Q3 is third in the header row B1:D1, so the second returns 3. INDEX reads B2:D4 at row 2, column 3, and B7 shows 130.

The two lists run in different directions, which is why they are separate ranges. A2:A4 is a column of regions and B1:D1 is a row of quarters. Give the quarter MATCH the region column and Q3 is not among the labels it searches, so the cell shows #N/A.

Both calls need the zero, since neither list is sorted. A wrong number from either one still produces a figure: swap the two MATCH calls and B7 reads 95, West's Q2. When a two-way answer is a number you did not expect, check each MATCH on its own before blaming INDEX.

errors.text: A region missing from A2:A4, or a quarter missing from B1:D1, leaves one of the two positions without a value.
The two MATCH calls went in the wrong order, so INDEX reads row 3 column 2 and returns 95.
A MATCH run over a range that reaches past the grid returns a position B2:D4 does not have.

docs.atWork: A budget grid with regions down the side and quarters across the top, read by label each month.
docs.outcome: Read one cell out of a grid by matching its row and column labels.

seo.title: Two-way INDEX MATCH in Excel
seo.description: One MATCH finds the South row, the other finds the Q3 column, and INDEX reads the cell they meet at. Swap the ranges and it gives #N/A, not a wrong number.
